angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 692,917 km at 127.04 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.8713 +/- 0.0130 mas (same row, RUWE 0.98): 127.04 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.996 +/- 0.015 solar radii from Johns et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of KELT-23 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158...78J/abstract): 692,917 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.944 +/- 0.06 solar masses from Johns et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of KELT-23 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158...78J/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5899 +/- 49 K from Johns et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of KELT-23 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158...78J/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Johns et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of KELT-23 A b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158...78J/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kelt-23-a.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.417, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
